subtopics.title: The Elements — What Economics Is Made Of

questions.question: Economics is best defined as the social science studying how:
options: People, businesses and governments use LIMITED resources to satisfy UNLIMITED needs and wants
Businesses maximise profit at any cost

questions.question: The four factors of production, paired correctly with their rewards, are:
options: Money, shares, loans and grants — all earning interest
Natural resources earn rent, labour earns wages, capital earns interest, entrepreneurship earns profit
Land earns profit, labour earns rent, capital earns wages, entrepreneurship earns interest
Only labour earns a reward; the rest are free

questions.question: Wants are called UNLIMITED because:
options: Shops never run out of stock
Everyone wants exactly the same things
Satisfying one want brings the next forward to replace it — the queue refills itself

subtopics.title: The Branches — How the Subject Divides

questions.question: Microeconomics studies:
options: Individual units — one household's budget, one firm's price, one market's equilibrium

questions.question: "One shop's bread price" versus "the national cost of living" illustrates:
options: Micro versus MACRO — the close-range question against the whole-economy question

questions.question: "The economy grew by nought comma nine percent last year" is a:
options: Normative statement — it judges what ought to be
POSITIVE statement — it describes what is and can be tested against evidence

questions.question: Development economics concentrates on:
options: Raising the welfare of poorer economies — a branch of special weight in Southern Africa

questions.question: The scientific loop economists follow is:
options: OBSERVATION, then HYPOTHESIS, then TESTING, then LAW or THEORY

questions.question: CETERIS PARIBUS means:
options: "All other things remaining equal" — the clause that isolates one relationship while everything else is held still in thought

questions.question: An INDEX, like the consumer price index, is:
options: A single number compressing thousands of observations into one summary

questions.question: Economic laws are called TENDENCIES rather than certainties because:
options: Economics studies people, who learn, adapt and react to predictions about themselves

questions.question: Economics is classified as a:
options: SOCIAL science that applies scientific method to human behaviour

questions.question: What Economics SHARES with the natural sciences:
options: Hypotheses, data, testing and the building of quantitative models
The ability to repeat experiments on whole countries

questions.question: What Economics can NEVER share with chemistry:
options: Controlled, repeatable experiments on its full subject matter — society cannot be held still

questions.question: Membership of the sciences matters for citizens because it means economic claims:
options: Must answer to EVIDENCE — ask for the data, the mechanism and the comparison before believing

questions.question: The whole subject in one line:
options: Everyone wants more than there is — so now what?
Money makes the world go round

questions.question: At the weekend car wash, the pressure hose is an example of:
options: CAPITAL — man-made equipment used in production, earning interest on the money tied up in it

questions.question: The aunt who set up the car wash and carried the risk that nobody would arrive earns:
"Why did the salon put braids up by thirty rand?" is a question for:
options: The CLOSE-UP lens — microeconomics, one decision-maker in one market

questions.question: All prices rising together across the country is called:
"Bus fare went up by two rand" versus "bus fare is a disgrace":
options: The first MEASURES and is positive; the second WISHES and is normative
The first is macro; the second is micro

questions.question: The test that sorts micro from macro:
options: Can you point at it from your gate? One firm or fare — micro; a nationwide total or average — macro

subtopics.title: Testing Like a Scientist, Watching People Like a Neighbour

questions.question: Noticing the tuckshop queue is longest on Mondays, guessing why, and watching three more Mondays is:
options: The scientific loop — observation, hypothesis, testing — run on daily life

questions.question: Ceteris paribus is needed because:
options: Real life changes many things at once — the clause isolates ONE thread so cause and effect can be seen

questions.question: Families stocking up BEFORE an announced petrol price increase shows that:
options: Petrol obeys the law of demand
People act on predictions about themselves — which is why economic laws stay tendencies

questions.question: Two economists disagreeing on the radio is best understood as:
options: The normal sound of a young science working on the hardest material there is — people
